raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #64746; review only the last commit ("Keep the MoE-LoRA shrink/expand intermediate in fp32 and round the output once"). Diff of that commit: 2 files, +95 / -3.

## Purpose

On the shrink/expand path the rank-sized intermediate (`x @ A^T`) is stored in bf16/fp16, and expand adds its result to the output in the 16-bit dtype. The LoRA delta is therefore rounded twice before it reaches the output, and its error is 1.2-2.2x the error of rounding the exact result once (kernel numbers below).

## Changes

- For batches of up to `FUSED_MOE_LORA_TWO_KERNEL_MAX_TOKENS` (256) tokens, and whenever `SPLIT_K > 1` (already the case since #64746), the shrink output is kept in fp32.
- Expand splits the fp32 value into a hi/lo pair of 16-bit values and runs two dots against the 16-bit B weights, so the intermediate is used at fp32 accuracy with 16-bit tensor-core MMA.
- Expand adds the LoRA delta to the output in fp32 (`FP32_ADD_INPUTS`, previously XPU only), so the output is rounded once.

Batches above 256 tokens on the one-shot kernel are unchanged.

## Kernel accuracy and cost

max |out - ref| / max |ref| against an fp64 reference, divided by the error from rounding the fp64 result to bf16 (1.0 = exact up to output rounding). 5 MoE shapes x rank 8/16/32/64 x max_loras 1/4 x w13/w2 = 80 problems per M:

| path | GB200 geomean | GB200 max |
|---|---:|---:|
| main, M 1-64 | 1.171 | 2.163 |
| #64746, M 1-64 | 1.289 | 2.163 |
| this PR, M 1-64 | **1.000** | **1.002** |
| main and #64746, M 96-256 | 1.349 | 1.986 |
| this PR, M 96-256 | **1.000** | **1.002** |

On H200 the earlier measurement of the same code gave 1.000 geomean / 1.002 max for M ≤ 256 (main 1.223 / 2.095).

Kernel time, E=128, top_k=4, hidden=6144, moe_intermediate=768, rank 32, max_loras 1, µs (same harness as #64746):

| M | GB200 w13 #64746 | this PR | GB200 w2 #64746 | this PR | H200 w13 #64746 | this PR | H200 w2 #64746 | this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8.2 | 8.2 | 5.2 | 5.3 | 8.1 | 8.4 | 5.4 | 5.5 |
| 8 | 15.2 | 15.6 | 9.6 | 11.6 | 17.7 | 18.4 | 12.1 | 12.5 |
| 64 | 32.0 | 32.8 | 21.3 | 24.0 | 39.7 | 40.3 | 26.4 | 29.0 |
| 256 | 34.5 | 35.3 | 27.1 | 30.2 | 43.8 | 44.4 | 33.6 | 37.1 |

Over the 80 problems it costs 1-6% geomean per batch size. The worst case is +24%, on the w2 expand of the DeepSeek-V3-like shape (N=7168, rank 16).

## Accuracy with a real LoRA

Setup:
- `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct` + `jeeejeee/olmoe-instruct-text2sql-spider` (rank 8, alpha 32; attention, router and per-expert MLP), bf16, 1 GPU.
- 24 prompts: the text2sql template from `tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py` with its 4 questions plus 20 more on the same schema. Continuations: 64 greedy tokens, generated once with main. Every build then scores the same 24 sequences with `prompt_logprobs` (6147 scored tokens).
- Reference: HF transformers 5.20 in fp32 with the adapter merged into the weights (`W += alpha/r * B @ A`, computed in fp64, for every adapter module including the router). PEFT is not used because the adapter stores per-expert keys while transformers 5 stores OLMoE experts as fused 3D tensors. A reference without the router LoRA is further from every vLLM build (0.079 vs 0.058 mean), so vLLM does apply it. A vLLM `dtype=float32` run fails at engine init and is not used.
- `max_num_batched_tokens` 64 / 256 / 8192 with chunked prefill, so every forward has ≤ 64 tokens, ≤ 256 tokens, or about 6.2k tokens (one-shot kernel in every build).
- "main" is e49ea84e9, "#64653", "#64746" are the parents in this stack. main and this PR were each run twice.

Mean |Δ logprob| against the fp32 reference, nats (max |Δ| in parentheses), default settings:

| GPU | tokens per forward | main | main, 2nd run | #64653 | #64746 | this PR | this PR, 2nd run |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GB200 | ≤ 64 | 0.0624 (1.11) | 0.0626 (1.11) | 0.0635 (1.11) | 0.0593 (1.32) | **0.0582** (1.10) | 0.0583 (1.10) |
| GB200 | ≤ 256 | 0.0576 (1.02) | 0.0575 (1.02) | 0.0579 (1.02) | 0.0573 (0.88) | 0.0593 (1.15) | 0.0592 (1.15) |
| GB200 | ~6.2k | 0.0582 (1.05) | 0.0601 (1.12) | 0.0596 (0.83) | 0.0579 (1.05) | 0.0581 (1.00) | 0.0577 (1.05) |
| H200 | ≤ 64 | 0.0574 (1.06) | 0.0573 (1.06) | 0.0576 (1.06) | 0.0545 (1.19) | **0.0549** (1.19) | 0.0546 (1.05) |
| H200 | ≤ 256 | 0.0584 (0.94) | 0.0584 (0.94) | 0.0587 (0.94) | 0.0592 (1.05) | 0.0603 (1.18) | 0.0600 (1.18) |
| H200 | ~6.2k | 0.0598 (0.95) | 0.0595 (0.95) | 0.0591 (0.95) | 0.0601 (0.95) | 0.0597 (0.95) | 0.0593 (0.95) |

Mean |Δ logprob| between builds directly (same tokens):

| GPU | tokens per forward | main vs main, 2nd run | main vs this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GB200 | ≤ 64 | 0.0164 | 0.0485 |
| GB200 | ≤ 256 | 0.0095 | 0.0455 |
| GB200 | ~6.2k | 0.0357 | 0.0267 |
| H200 | ≤ 64 | 0.0151 | 0.0446 |
| H200 | ≤ 256 | 0.0138 | 0.0511 |
| H200 | ~6.2k | 0.0086 | 0.0078 |

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (deterministic; `SPLIT_K = 1`):

| GPU | tokens per forward | main | #64653 | #64746 | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GB200 | ≤ 64 | 0.0727 | 0.0727 | 0.0727 | **0.0706** |
| GB200 | ≤ 256 | 0.0730 | 0.0730 | 0.0730 | **0.0707** |
| GB200 | ~6.2k | 0.0713 | 0.0713 | - | 0.0713 |
| H200 | ≤ 64 | 0.0766 | 0.0766 | 0.0766 | **0.0668** |
| H200 | ≤ 256 | 0.0766 | 0.0766 | 0.0766 | **0.0668** |
| H200 | ~6.2k | 0.0766 | 0.0766 | - | 0.0766 |

What this shows:
- The bf16 model's error against fp32 (about 0.06 nats mean, about 1 nat max) comes mostly from the rest of the model. Without batch invariance, two runs of the same build already differ by 0.01-0.04 nats mean, and every kernel change moves the end-to-end error by a few percent in either direction. In default mode this PR is 7% / 4% lower than main at ≤ 64 tokens and 3% higher at ≤ 256 tokens (GB200 / H200); at about 6.2k tokens it matches main, as expected since the one-shot kernel is unchanged.
- With batch invariance the runs are deterministic. #64653 and #64746 give logprobs bit-identical to main, and this PR lowers the mean error by 3% (GB200) and 13% (H200) for batches of up to 256 tokens, and is bit-identical to main above 256 tokens.

## Test Plan

New `test_fused_moe_lora_two_kernel_matches_rounded_reference` (split-K 1/4/8, naive and sorted, bf16 and fp16, with a residual in the output) requires the error to be within 1.01x of the output-rounding floor.

## Test Result

- The 4 new cases fail on #64746 (e.g. error 0.00339 vs a floor of 0.00194) and pass with this PR.
- `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` on 1 GPU: 469 passed, 12 skipped (GB200 and H200); `-k fully_sharded` on 2 GPUs (H200): 12 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` (0.14.0) clean; mypy reports no new errors on the changed files.

+def get_fused_moe_lora_two_kernel_config(
+    op_type: str,
+    num_tokens: int,
+    top_k: int,

+    max_loras: int,

+) -> dict[str, int | None]:
+    device = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()

+    if current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
+        max_shared_memory = get_max_shared_memory_bytes(device)
+    return _fused_moe_lora_two_kernel_config(
+        op_type,

+@functools.lru_cache
+def _fused_moe_lora_two_kernel_config(
+    op_type: str,
+    num_tokens: int,
+    top_k: int,
+    num_experts: int,
+    max_loras: int,
+    num_slices: int,
+    in_features: int,
+    out_features: int,
+    rank: int,
+    num_sms: int,
+    max_shared_memory: int,
+) -> dict[str, int | None]:
+    block_m = 16
+    pairs = num_tokens * top_k
+    m_blocks = max(1, min(pairs, max_loras * num_experts + pairs // block_m))
+    num_stages = 2 if current_platform.is_rocm() else 3
+    if op_type.endswith("shrink"):
+        block_n = max(16, min(64, next_power_of_2(rank)))
+        programs = m_blocks * num_slices * cdiv(rank, block_n)
+        split_k = min(16, max(1, prev_power_of_2(2 * num_sms // programs)))
+        block_k = max(64, min(256, prev_power_of_2(in_features // split_k)))
+        while (
+            block_k > 64
+            and max_shared_memory
+            and num_stages * (block_m + block_n) * block_k * 2 > max_shared_memory
+        ):
+            block_k //= 2
+        split_k = max(split_k, next_power_of_2(cdiv(in_features, 16 * block_k)))
+        split_k = min(split_k, 16, max(1, prev_power_of_2(in_features // block_k)))
+        return {
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_M": block_m,
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_N": block_n,
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_K": block_k,
+            "GROUP_SIZE_M": 1,
+            "SPLIT_K": 1 if is_batch_invariant else split_k,
+            "num_warps": 4,
+            "num_stages": num_stages,
+        }
+    block_n = 256
+    while block_n > 64 and m_blocks * num_slices * cdiv(out_features, block_n) < (
+        num_sms
+    ):
+        block_n //= 2
+    return {
+        "BLOCK_SIZE_M": block_m,
+        "BLOCK_SIZE_N": block_n,
+        "BLOCK_SIZE_K": max(16, min(32, next_power_of_2(rank))),
+        "GROUP_SIZE_M": 1,
+        "SPLIT_K": 1,
+        "num_warps": 4,
+        "num_stages": 2,
+    }
